transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I came in because things got… weirdly intense. I’d barely even finished settling into my new apartment—there are still boxes in the corner, and I keep meaning to buy actual curtains instead of using that temporary paper shade thing—and then suddenly I was saying yes to all these mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes, and deciding I needed to redo my entire portfolio.

It felt like I had to fix my whole life in one sprint, like everything had to happen right now. At first it seemed productive, but then it started feeling like… a lot.
During this intense period, did you feel like you needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah… I mean, I didn’t think of it that way at the time, because I kept telling myself I was just finally using my mornings better. But for several nights I was only sleeping maybe three or four hours, and I’d wake up like, okay, great, I’m fine, I should get ahead while it’s quiet.

Which is funny because normally if my upstairs neighbor so much as drops a shoe at midnight I’m useless the next day, but then I was just… up, making coffee way too early and opening design files like it was totally normal.
During that time, did you feel unusually euphoric or unusually irritable?

Yeah… both, I think. Earlier this month I had these moments where I felt almost electric, like everything was finally clicking and I was in this weirdly upbeat, shiny mood.

But then the tiniest thing would flip it. Like a contractor taking too long to answer about something in the apartment, or my sister not replying fast enough—I snapped at them like they were personally standing in the way of my whole life. Which, saying it out loud, sounds dramatic, because it was probably just normal delays. I just really didn’t experience it that way in the moment.
During this intense period, did you ever believe things that other people said weren’t true?

I don’t think so? I mean, not like… believing the TV was sending me messages or anything like that.

I was probably overly convinced that certain things had to happen right away, like the apartment stuff and work stuff, but if someone pushed back, I don’t think I was believing something unreal. I’d get annoyed and then start explaining the whole logic of it, which—my sister would say I do even when I’m not stressed, because apparently I turn every disagreement into a slide deck. But no, I don’t think people were telling me, “That’s not true,” and I was holding onto some totally false belief.
During that intense period, were you hospitalized because of it?

No, I wasn’t hospitalized. It didn’t get to that point.

I mean, I did have that thing where I was sort of barreling through my days and acting like I had twelve tabs open in my brain, which I guess is basically my actual laptop most of the time too. But nobody took me to the hospital or told me I needed to go, and I didn’t go on my own.
During that intense period, did it cause serious problems in your work or relationships?

Yeah… I think it did, unfortunately. Work especially. I missed a design review, which is not like missing some optional check-in—there were people waiting on me and I just… I don’t know, I had my notes in three different places and thought I had the time wrong, or maybe I convinced myself I could still pull it together last minute.

And then with people, I’ve kind of been avoiding my friends and my family. Not because they did anything, really. I just feel embarrassed. Like I’ve been scattered and unreliable lately, and then every text feels like I have to explain the whole mess, and then I don’t answer, which makes it worse. So… yeah, it has caused problems.
During that same period, did you also feel depressed most of the day?

Yeah… most of the day, I think. It’s not always dramatic, like I’m sobbing or anything, but lately I wake up and there’s this heavy, gray feeling in my chest.

And then I’ll be standing in the kitchen and the apartment is quiet, nothing is actually wrong in that exact moment, and I’ll see, like, a coffee mug sitting in the sink and suddenly feel like I could cry over it. Which sounds ridiculous when I say it out loud, because it’s just a mug, but… yeah. That feeling has been there a lot.
About how many days in a row did this unusually energized, sped-up period last?

It’s hard for me to separate it cleanly into, like, “these exact number of days,” because it sort of came with all the apartment stuff. Since I moved into this place—about a month ago—that whole intense up-and-down thing has been going on.

I keep thinking, maybe it started the week I was still unpacking, because I had boxes everywhere and I was labeling cables for some reason instead of doing normal moving tasks… sorry, that’s not really the point. But yeah, roughly since I moved in, so about a month.
During that period, were you talking more than usual or feeling pressure to keep talking?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I know I can ramble when I’m nervous—like even right now, I’m probably doing it. And with work stuff, I’ll sometimes over-explain design decisions because I’m trying to make sure people don’t misunderstand the wireframes or the user flow or… sorry.

But whether it was more than usual during that period, or like I felt forced to keep talking, I don’t know. I didn’t really notice that specifically.
During that month, did your elevated or irritable mood make you unable to function in your normal day-to-day life?

Yeah… I mean, I was still technically functioning, like I wasn’t just in bed all day or anything, but it definitely started messing things up.

I missed a design review, which is not really like me. I had the calendar invite and everything, and then somehow I was doing… I don’t even know, reorganizing files or trying to fix some tiny layout issue that didn’t need fixing, and by the time I realized, the meeting was over. I felt so stupid about it.

And I’ve been kind of dodging people too—friends, my sister, my parents—because I’m embarrassed. I feel like I’ve seemed really scattered and unreliable lately, and I don’t want to have to explain why I’m being weird or flaky. So… yeah, not completely unable to function, but it’s definitely affected my day-to-day life.
While you were feeling unusually energized and needing less sleep, were you also feeling depressed at the same time?

Yeah… I think so. It’s weird, because I can be kind of wired, like my body won’t settle, but emotionally it’s not happy energy.

Lately I’ll wake up and there’s just this heavy, gray feeling in my chest. And even if the apartment is totally quiet and nothing bad is actually happening, I’ll see something stupid, like a coffee mug sitting in the sink, and feel like I could cry over it. Which sounds dramatic when I say it out loud, but that’s how it’s been.
